title: Set 110

sentences.ko: 다들 우리한테 왜 아직도 집 안 사고 세 살고 있냐고 물어보는데, 나도 딱히 할 말이 없으니까 그냥 계속 알아보는 중이라고만 했어. 그러다 삼촌이 휴대폰을 꺼내서 자기 동네 집값이 얼마인지 보여 주더라고, 다들 바로 옆에 앉아서 듣고 있는데. 두 시에 들어갔다가 네 시에는 다시 차에 타 있었어.
sentences.text: Every one of them wanted to know why we're still renting, and I don't really have a good answer for that, so I just kept saying we're looking. And then my uncle pulled his phone out to show me what houses go for out by him, with everybody sitting right there listening. I walked in at two and I was back in my car by four.

alts.text: Literally all of them asked why we're still renting, and I don't really have a good answer for that, so I just kept going we're looking. Then my uncle pulls out his phone to show me what houses cost out by him, with everybody sitting right there listening. I got there at two and I was back in my car by four.

Each of them asked why we are still renting, and I do not really have a good answer for that, so I simply kept saying that we are looking. Then my uncle took out his phone to show me what houses sell for in his area, with everyone sitting right there listening. I arrived at two and I was back in my car by four.

sentences.note: **what houses go for** 는 집이 얼마에 팔리는지를 말할 때 쓰는 표현입니다. 값을 말할 때 cost 대신 go for 를 쓰면 훨씬 자연스럽습니다. **I don't really have a good answer for that** 은 딱히 할 말이 없다고 얼버무릴 때 그대로 쓰는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 친척들 모인 자리에서 질문 공세 받은 얘기

sentences.ko: 퇴근하고 헬스장 가려고 했는데 점심을 세 시쯤에 먹는 바람에 여섯 시에도 아직 배가 불렀어. 나는 배부를 때 뭘 들면 속이 울렁거려서 못 하거든. 그래서 대신 아침에 출근 전에 가자고 마음먹었지. 근데 그 시간에 못 일어날 거 나도 이미 알아.
sentences.text: I was going to go to the gym after work, but I ended up eating lunch at like three, so by six I was still full, and I can't lift anything on a full stomach without feeling sick. So I told myself I'd go in the morning before work instead. I already know I'm not getting up for that.

alts.text: I meant to hit the gym after work, but lunch didn't happen till like three, so at six I was still full, and I can't lift anything on a full stomach without feeling sick. So I told myself I'd just go in the morning before work. I already know I'm not getting up for that.

I had intended to go to the gym after work, but I ended up eating lunch at around three, so by six I was still full, and I cannot lift anything on a full stomach without feeling ill. I therefore told myself that I would go in the morning before work instead. I already know that I will not be getting up for that.

sentences.note: **on a full stomach** 는 배가 부른 상태에서라는 뜻으로, 운동이나 수영 얘기에 자주 붙습니다. **I ended up eating lunch at like three** 처럼 end up -ing 는 하려던 것과 다르게 결국 그렇게 됐다는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 운동 가려다 말게 된 핑계 대기

sentences.ko: 내 룸메이트 오빠인데, 너보다 훨씬 말수가 적어. 근데 이상한 쪽으로 그런 게 아니라 그냥 남이 말하게 두는 편이야. 요리도 하고 강아지도 키우고, 이혼한 지는 이 년쯤 됐어. 이건 저녁 먹다가 알게 되면 좀 그러니까 지금 미리 말해 두는 거야. 너 진짜 마음에 들어 할 것 같은데. 번호 줄까, 아니면 사진 먼저 볼래?
sentences.text: Okay, so he's my roommate's older brother, and he's a lot quieter than you are, but not in a weird way, he just lets other people talk. He cooks, he's got a dog, and he's been divorced for about two years, which I'm telling you now so you don't find out at dinner. I think you'd actually like him. Do you want me to give him your number, or do you want to see a picture first?

alts.text: So, my roommate's got an older brother, and he's way quieter than you, but not in a weird way, he just lets other people talk. He cooks, he's got a dog, and he's been divorced like two years, which I'm telling you now so you don't find out at dinner. I really think you'd like him. Want me to give him your number, or do you wanna see a picture first?

He is my roommate's older brother, and he is considerably quieter than you are, though not in an odd way, he simply lets other people talk. He cooks, he has a dog, and he has been divorced for about two years, which I am mentioning now so that you do not find out at dinner. I think you would genuinely like him. Would you like me to give him your number, or would you prefer to see a picture first?

sentences.note: **not in a weird way** 는 방금 한 말이 흉보는 소리로 들릴까 봐 바로 뒤에 덧붙이는 말입니다. **he's been divorced for about two years** 처럼 이혼한 지 얼마가 됐다는 말은 현재완료로 합니다.
sentences.situation: 친구 소개팅 주선하면서 상대가 어떤 사람인지 설명하기

sentences.ko: 처음 두 시즌은 올라오는 날 밤에 안 자고 기다렸다가 봤는데, 지금은 보는 내내 휴대폰만 봐. 아무도 뭘 하질 않고 그냥 둘러앉아서 서로 기분이 어떤지 얘기만 하거든. 우리 형은 6화쯤부터 다시 살아난다고 우기니까 거기까지는 봐 줄까 싶기도 해. 근데 나는 다시 살아날 것 같지 않아.
sentences.text: The first couple seasons I'd stay up and watch it the night it came out, and now I'm on my phone the whole time, because nobody does anything anymore, they just sit around telling each other how they feel. My brother swears it picks back up around episode six, so I might give it that long. I really don't think it picks back up.

alts.text: First two seasons I'd be up watching it the night it dropped, and now I'm on my phone the whole time, cause nobody does anything anymore, they just sit around telling each other how they feel. My brother swears it picks back up around episode six, so I might give it that long. I really don't think it picks back up.

For the first couple of seasons I would stay up and watch it the night it was released, and now I am on my phone the entire time, because nobody does anything anymore, they simply sit around telling each other how they feel. My brother insists that it picks back up around episode six, so I may give it that long. I really do not think it picks back up.

sentences.note: **it picks back up** 은 늘어졌던 이야기가 다시 재미있어진다는 뜻입니다. **My brother swears** 의 swears 는 맹세한다기보다 확신에 차서 우긴다는 뜻으로 쓰입니다.

sentences.ko: 카페에 갔더니 여덟 명쯤 되는 무리가 가운데 테이블을 전부 붙여 놔서 앉을 자리가 없었어. 문 바로 옆에 있는 스툴 하나 빼고는. 누가 일어나나 싶어서 카운터 옆에서 몇 분 기다렸는데, 그냥 서 있는 게 좀 뻘쭘해져서 결국 테이크아웃 했어. 두 시쯤부터 앉아서 쉴 생각만 하고 있었는데.
sentences.text: I got to the coffee place and some group of like eight people had pushed all the tables together in the middle, so there was nowhere to sit unless I wanted the one stool right by the door. I waited by the counter a few minutes to see if anybody would get up, and then I felt strange just standing there, so I got my coffee to go. I'd been looking forward to sitting down since about two o'clock.

alts.text: So I show up at the coffee place and there's like eight people who'd shoved all the tables together in the middle, so there was nowhere to sit unless I wanted the one stool right by the door. I hung around by the counter a few minutes to see if anybody would get up, and then I felt weird just standing there, so I got mine to go. I'd been looking forward to sitting down since like two o'clock.

I arrived at the coffee shop and a group of about eight people had pushed all of the tables together in the middle, so there was nowhere to sit unless I wanted the single stool right beside the door. I waited by the counter for a few minutes to see whether anyone would get up, and then I felt odd simply standing there, so I ordered my coffee to go. I had been looking forward to sitting down since about two o'clock.

sentences.note: **got my coffee to go** 의 to go 는 포장해서 가져간다는 뜻입니다. 매장에서 먹을 때는 for here 라고 합니다. **I'd been looking forward to sitting down** 은 아까부터 계속 기다려 왔다는 뜻으로, 앞선 시점부터 이어진 일이라 had been 을 씁니다.

reviewed: 1번 formal 의 "Every single one of them" 은 격식체가 아니라 강조하는 구어라서 "Each of them asked" 로 바꿨다.
1번 한국어의 "집 안 사고 세로 사냐" 가 어색해서 "아직도 집 안 사고 세 살고 있냐" 로 다듬고, 뒤 문장도 말끝을 자연스럽게 손봤다.
2번 casual 이 text 와 시작이 사실상 같았다(I was going to go / I was gonna). "I meant to hit the gym ... but lunch didn't happen till like three" 로 다르게 시작하도록 고쳤다.
3번 casual 도 text 와 앞부분이 그대로 겹쳤다(So he's my roommate's ... brother). "So, my roommate's got an older brother" 로 구조를 바꿨다.
4번 한국어의 "육 회" 는 한국 사람이 쓰지 않는 말이라 "6화" 로 고쳤다.
4번 casual 도 앞부분이 text 와 겹쳐서 "First two seasons I'd be up watching it the night it dropped" 로 바꿨다.
